What does a birthday party bus cost in Scottsdale?

Scottsdale Sprinters prices a birthday by the hour against a published minimum, so the 28-seat Party Bus (28 Pax) starts at $1,000, which is $250 an hour across its 4-hour minimum, before 8% tax. Across a full bus that floor is about $36 a seat. The same arithmetic runs on every unit. The Limo Party Sprinter (16 Pax) and the Limo Party Sprinter (12-13 Pax) share $175, so both open at $700; the Ultra Luxury Party Sprinter opens at $1,000 and the Pink Hummer Limo at $1,180. Those are the current published hourly rates and minimums. Hours past the minimum bill at the same rate. The published evening shape is 7 hours, of which 1 is free, so it bills as 6: $1,050 on a party Sprinter, $1,500 on the bus, $1,770 on the limousine. There is no birthday package to buy.

How does a birthday evening in Old Town Scottsdale actually run?

A birthday booking is hours with a chauffeur, not a route we sell you: the published evening is 7 hours, and the clock runs from the first pickup to the last drop-off. All party units hold that window, and stops inside it are free. The pickup instruction the bus page publishes: "A party bus needs room to stand and turn, so give us a street address with curb space rather than a driveway or a parking structure, and one phone we call for the group. List every stop on the reservation up front — stops on an hourly charter cost nothing." The window is the product: "Hourly charters start at four hours. The vehicle stays with your group for the whole booked window, so the clock runs from pickup to the last drop-off, not per stop. Anything the online quote cannot price — an unusual route, a multi-vehicle movement, a vehicle we hold for request only — goes to the reservations desk and comes back as a written quote before any card is charged." What the chauffeur handles: "Ask your chauffeur for anything. Stops, temperature, volume, a photo. Really." Where a commercial vehicle may legally stop is the property's call.

What changes for a 21st, 30th, 40th or 50th birthday?

Operationally, nothing: all 4 milestones book the same party units, at the same published rates, against the same 4-hour minimum, under one page of house rules. What changes is the group size and the shape of the evening, and both are priced the same way. A 21st is usually the largest headcount, which is the Party Bus (28 Pax)'s case: 28 seats, cheapest per head at $36 a seat. A 30th or a 40th runs dinner-sized, where the Limo Party Sprinter (16 Pax) at $700 covers it without buying floor nobody uses. A 50th is the arrival rather than the crawl. That is the Pink Hummer Limo's argument at $295 an hour: 18 seats, $1,180 to start, $66 a seat. No milestone carries its own package, decoration list or minimum, because none is published.

What are the rules for a sweet 16 party bus?

A sweet sixteen books exactly like every other birthday here — the same party units, the same 4-hour minimum, the same published rates — and the 2 rules that decide the rest are the house alcohol rules, quoted below word for word rather than summarised. The rules as published: "Passengers 21 and over bring their own alcohol, and we do not sell it. Arizona vehicle-for-hire open-container policy, A.R.S. § 4-251, allows it, and if anyone under 21 rides, no alcohol comes on that trip." and "No underage drinking. Anyone under 21 stays on soft drinks." Those 2 sentences are the site's whole age policy, and they apply on every trip. Beyond them this page states nothing, deliberately. Scottsdale Sprinters publishes no chaperone ratio, no adult-to-guest count, no separate under-21 booking product and no alcohol-free package, so none is claimed here. A group with guests under 21 should say so when requesting the quote and have the arrangements confirmed in writing. Nothing else changes: the $50 transfer stop fee and the 3 fee-bearing rules are identical, and so is this: "Be kind to your chauffeur. They are the reason everyone gets home."

What is included on board, and how is the quote built?

One page of house rules governs every trip here, whatever the vehicle, and 3 of those rules carry a stated fee. Drinking is allowed for guests 21 and over, eating is not, and smoking or vaping of any kind carries a $1,500 fee no birthday booking waives. What comes with the vehicle: "Bottled water is on board and it is the only complimentary amenity; everything else is an add-on you choose at checkout." Eating is a separate rule: "No eating or food inside the vehicle. Drinks are fine; snacks wait for the next stop." "No smoking or vaping of any kind. The smell does not leave, so this one carries a fee." ($1,500). "Keep the drinks in the cups. Minor spills are fine; a can or two on the floor counts as excessive and carries a cleaning fee." ($450). "If someone gets sick in the vehicle, we have to deep clean it, and that carries a cleaning fee. Pace yourselves." ($450). Condition is documented, not argued afterwards. "Before every trip your chauffeur takes a documented set of photos of the interior. They are for our internal records only." "You authorize us to charge the card on file for damage beyond normal use. We will never charge for damage without telling you first, with the photos, so there are no surprises." The quote is arithmetic you can check: the published rate, the billable hours, 8% Arizona tax and, on a card, the 50% deposit.
